blurb: Big hair, bigger phones: the tech, fads and moments of the 1980s

questions.q: Apple's famous '1984' Super Bowl ad introduced which computer?
questions.fact: It was directed by Ridley Scott, of Alien and Blade Runner fame, and aired during Super Bowl XVIII.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc. (Macintosh Jan 24, 1984; '1984' ad by Ridley Scott, Super Bowl XVIII)

questions.q: In the 80s home-video format war, VHS beat which Sony format?
questions.fact: VHS was developed by JVC; Sony had launched Betamax back in 1975.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony (Betamax 1975; VHS developed by JVC). Other options are non-Sony formats.

questions.q: The DynaTAC 8000X, the first commercial handheld cellphone, was approved for sale in which year?
questions.fact: Motorola's phone won FCC approval in September 1983, about a decade after the first handheld cellphone call.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorola (FCC approved DynaTAC 8000X Sept 1983); wiki/Mobile_phone (first handheld call April 3, 1973)

questions.q: Which band's 1985 album 'Brothers in Arms' was the first to sell a million copies on CD?
questions.fact: It was also the first album to sell more copies on CD than on vinyl LP.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brothers_in_Arms_(album) ('first album to sell one million copies in the CD format and to outsell its LP version')

questions.q: In E.T. (1982), Elliott lures the alien with a trail of which candy?
questions.fact: The film gave a big sales boost to Reese's Pieces, which had been introduced just four years earlier, in 1978.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reese%27s_Pieces (US launch Sept 1978; Mars declined the E.T. placement; sales up as much as 300%)

questions.q: Swatch, the colorful plastic watch craze of the 1980s, came from which country?
questions.fact: Launched in 1983, the low-cost Swatch helped revive the Swiss watch industry.
questions.src: swissinfo.ch 'The Swatch celebrates its 20th birthday' (launched in Zurich March 1, 1983; 'did much to rescue the Swiss watch industry')

questions.q: Which 1983 film made ripped, off-the-shoulder sweatshirts a fashion craze?
questions.fact: Star Jennifer Beals said her sweatshirt shrank in the dryer, so she simply cut around the neck hole.
questions.src: entertainment.time.com 'What a Feeling: 10 Legacies of Flashdance' (ripped-shoulder clothing slide; Beals: sweatshirt stayed in the dryer too long, she cut around the hole). Footloose 1984, Fame 1980, Dirty Dancing 1987.

questions.q: The Trapper Keeper, an 80s school-binder craze, was made by which company?
questions.fact: Mead first test-marketed the Trapper Keeper in Wichita, Kansas, in August 1978.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapper_Keeper (made by Mead; initial market Wichita, Kansas, August 1978)

questions.q: In 1985, which soda brand changed its famous formula, then brought the original back 79 days later?
questions.fact: The returning original was sold as 'Coca-Cola Classic,' while the new formula became known as New Coke.
questions.src: history.com This Day in History (New Coke April 23, 1985; original returned July 11, 1985, '79 days after the release of New Coke')

questions.q: The 1985 Live Aid benefit concerts were held in London and which US city?
questions.fact: Both shows took place on July 13, 1985, at London's Wembley Stadium and Philadelphia's JFK Stadium.
questions.src: britannica.com/event/Live-Aid; billypenn.com (July 13, 1985, Wembley Stadium London and JFK Stadium Philadelphia)

questions.q: Kirk Gibson's famous limping home run in the 1988 World Series was for which team?
questions.fact: His pinch-hit, game-winning homer in Game 1 was his only plate appearance of the Series.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirk_Gibson%27s_1988_World_Series_home_run ('his only plate appearance of the series'; Dodgers vs A's, off Dennis Eckersley)

questions.q: Which country hosted the 1986 FIFA World Cup, won by Argentina?
questions.fact: Colombia was the original host but withdrew, so Mexico became the first nation to host the World Cup twice.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_FIFA_World_Cup (Colombia withdrew Nov 1982; Mexico 'became the first nation to host two World Cups'; Argentina won)

blurb: Dial-up, grunge and the Macarena: the 1990s on one board

questions.q: Which Microsoft system, launched in 1995, introduced the Start button?
questions.fact: Its launch ads used the Rolling Stones song 'Start Me Up,' a nod to the new Start button.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_95 (GA Aug 24, 1995; introduced Start menu and taskbar; 'Start Me Up' ad)

questions.q: The 'Y2K bug' scare came from old computers storing years with how many digits?
questions.fact: Programs that saved 1999 as '99' risked reading '00' as 1900 instead of 2000.
questions.src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook-certain: two-digit year storage behind the Y2K bug)

questions.q: The first text message, sent in the UK in December 1992, said what?
questions.fact: Engineer Neil Papworth typed it on a computer and sent it to the phone of Vodafone's Richard Jarvis.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SMS (Dec 3, 1992, Papworth of Sema Group to Richard Jarvis of Vodafone)

questions.q: In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue computer beat which world chess champion in a match?
questions.fact: Kasparov had beaten an earlier version of Deep Blue in their first match, in 1996.
questions.src: history.com 'Kasparov defeats chess-playing computer' (Feb 1996 match); chessbase.com '25 years ago: Deep Blue beats Kasparov' (1997 rematch)

questions.q: The 90s grunge look of flannel and ripped jeans came out of which city's music scene?
questions.fact: Bands like Nirvana, Pearl Jam and Soundgarden carried the Seattle sound around the world.
questions.src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook-certain: Seattle grunge scene; Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Soundgarden)

questions.q: Los del Rio, the duo behind the 1990s dance craze 'Macarena,' come from which country?
questions.fact: A remix by the Bayside Boys turned it into a No. 1 hit in the US in 1996.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macarena (Spanish duo Los del Rio; Bayside Boys remix No. 1 on the Hot 100 from August 1996 for 14 weeks)

questions.q: The 'Magic Eye' book craze of the 1990s hid what kind of picture inside colorful patterns?
questions.fact: The pictures are autostereograms: relax your focus and a 3D shape seems to float off the page.
questions.src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook-certain: Magic Eye autostereograms)

questions.q: The 90s POG craze took its name from a Hawaiian juice of passion fruit, orange and what?
questions.fact: Maui's Haleakala Dairy created the juice in 1971 and gave away caps printed with the POG logo.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pog_(drink) (passionfruit-orange-guava; created 1971 by Mary Soon for Haleakala Dairy, Maui; dairy gave away POG-logo caps; craze began 1991)

questions.q: Which film saga returned to theaters in 1999 with 'The Phantom Menace'?
questions.fact: It opened on May 19, 1999, almost 16 years after Return of the Jedi.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars:_Episode_I_%E2%80%93_The_Phantom_Menace (US release May 19, 1999, 'almost 16 years after the premiere of Return of the Jedi')

questions.q: When Johnny Carson retired in 1992, who took over as host of The Tonight Show?
questions.fact: David Letterman, seen by many as Carson's natural successor, left NBC for CBS in 1993.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_with_Jay_Leno (debuted May 25, 1992, three days after Carson retired; Letterman 'considered by many as the natural successor'; left NBC June 1993, joined CBS August 1993)

questions.q: In 1996, Starbucks opened its first store outside North America in which city?
questions.fact: The store opened in August 1996 in Tokyo's Ginza shopping district.
questions.src: tastingtable.com/1854774 (first store outside North America opened in Tokyo in August 1996, in the Ginza shopping district)

questions.q: After his first NBA retirement, Michael Jordan played minor league baseball in 1994 for which team?
questions.fact: The Barons were a Double-A farm team of the Chicago White Sox, whose owner also owned the Bulls.
questions.src: nbcsports.com oral history of Jordan's baseball career (#45 of the Birmingham Barons, 1994). Barons as White Sox Double-A club and Reinsdorf owning both teams: textbook.

blurb: iPods, BlackBerrys and red envelopes: the 2000s on rewind

questions.q: Apple's first iPod, in 2001, promised how many songs in your pocket?
questions.fact: A copywriter named it after the line 'Open the pod bay doors' from 2001: A Space Odyssey.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPod (Nov 10, 2001; '1,000 songs in your pocket'; Vinnie Chieco name origin)

questions.q: BlackBerry phones, famous for their tiny keyboards, were made in which country?
questions.fact: Maker Research In Motion was based in Waterloo, Ontario; the first BlackBerry was a 1999 email pager.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlackBerry (RIM, Waterloo, Ontario; BlackBerry 850 pager Jan 19, 1999)

questions.q: The first iPhone went on sale in the US in June of which year?
questions.fact: Steve Jobs unveiled it on January 9, 2007, and it reached stores on June 29.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Inc.

questions.q: Which disc format beat HD DVD in the 2000s battle over high-definition movies?
questions.fact: Sony backed Blu-ray, and HD DVD's main supporter, Toshiba, gave up the fight in February 2008.
questions.src: engadget.com / cnn.com / aljazeera.com, Feb 19, 2008 (Toshiba drops HD DVD; Blu-ray wins). Sony backing Blu-ray is textbook.

questions.q: Netflix's DVD-by-mail service sent discs in envelopes of what color?
questions.fact: Netflix mailed its last DVDs in September 2023, 25 years after the service began.
questions.src: tweaktown.com/news/91156 (final red-envelope DVDs mailed Sept 29, 2023; DVD service began 25 years earlier)

questions.q: The Snuggie, a TV-ad sensation of 2008, was a blanket with what added?
questions.fact: Sleeved blankets like the Slanket were sold earlier, but the Snuggie's memorable ads made it a craze.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeved_blanket (Snuggie TV campaign autumn 2008; Freedom Blanket sold from 2005, Slanket launched 2006)

questions.q: YouTube's first video, 'Me at the zoo' (2005), was filmed at the zoo in which city?
questions.fact: Co-founder Jawed Karim posted the 19-second clip, which shows him standing in front of elephants.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me_at_the_zoo (San Diego Zoo; Jawed Karim in front of two elephants; 19 seconds; April 23, 2005)

questions.q: Crocs foam clogs made their 2002 debut at what kind of event?
questions.fact: Their first model was called the Beach, and all 200 pairs reportedly sold out at the Fort Lauderdale show.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crocs ('In 2002, Crocs unveiled their first model, the Beach, at the Fort Lauderdale Boat Show in Florida'; 200 pairs reportedly sold out)

questions.q: Which new currency went into circulation as cash in 12 European countries in 2002?
questions.fact: The euro had existed since 1999, but only electronically, before the notes and coins arrived.
questions.src: ecb.europa.eu euro changeover 2002 page (notes and coins introduced Jan 1, 2002 in 12 countries). Euro as non-cash currency from Jan 1999 is textbook.

questions.q: Facebook launched in 2004 as a site for students at which university?
questions.fact: It started as 'TheFacebook' and opened to anyone 13 or older in September 2006.
questions.src: Wikipedia 'Facebook' (copy at solarspell-dls.sfis.asu.edu): Thefacebook launched Feb 4, 2004 for Harvard students; opened Sept 26, 2006 to everyone 13 and older

questions.q: The London Eye, which opened in 2000, was originally called what?
questions.fact: At 443 feet, it was the world's tallest Ferris wheel until China's Star of Nanchang passed it in 2006.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Eye ('originally the Millennium Wheel'; opened to the paying public March 9, 2000; 135 m / 443 ft; tallest Ferris wheel until the Star of Nanchang in 2006)

questions.q: In 2001, the Seattle Mariners tied the major league record for regular-season wins. How many did they win?
questions.fact: They matched the 1906 Chicago Cubs, who won 116 games in a season of only 152 games.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Seattle_Mariners_season (116-46, 'tying the major league record for wins in the modern era'; 1906 Cubs did it in a 152-game season). Ichiro's 2001 MVP is already used in sports-legends, so kept out of the fact.

blurb: Disco suits, mood rings and floppy disks: a trip through the 1970s

questions.q: Sony's Walkman portable cassette player first went on sale in which year?
questions.fact: The first model, the TPS-L2, had two headphone jacks so two people could listen at once.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony (Walkman 1979); maketecheasier.com (first 1979 Walkman had a second headphone jack at Akio Morita's insistence); walkman-archive.com TPS-L2 page

questions.q: In the 1970s CB radio craze, what did CB stand for?
questions.fact: C.W. McCall's trucker song 'Convoy,' a No. 1 hit in early 1976, helped fuel the fad.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_(song) ('capitalized on the fad for citizens band (CB) radio'; one week at No. 1 on the pop chart in its 1975-76 run)

questions.q: In 1971, Ray Tomlinson sent the first networked email and chose which symbol for addresses?
questions.fact: He chose @ because no one used it in computing and it already meant 'at,' as in a user at a computer.
questions.src: maketecheasier.com/why-email-uses-at-symbol (Tomlinson, 1971; @ was unused in computing and 'already meant, in commercial English, at')

questions.q: IBM's first floppy disks, introduced in the early 1970s, measured how many inches across?
questions.fact: The smaller 5.25-inch floppy arrived in 1976, followed by the 3.5-inch disk in the 1980s.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floppy_disk (IBM's first floppies, 1971, were 8 inches; Shugart 5.25-inch in 1976; 3.5-inch drives first shipped 1983)

questions.q: John Travolta's white disco suit is the iconic look from which 1977 film?
questions.fact: The role earned Travolta his first Academy Award nomination, for Best Actor.
questions.src: tcm.com Critics' Corner: Saturday Night Fever (Travolta nominated for Best Actor; 'his first ever nomination')

questions.q: 1970s mood rings changed color in response to what?
questions.fact: The stones held heat-sensitive liquid crystals that shift color as temperature changes.
questions.src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook-certain: thermochromic liquid crystals)

questions.q: Bell-bottom pants borrowed their flared shape from the uniforms of which workers?
questions.fact: Navy sailors wore them for generations; the wide legs were said to be easy to roll up for scrubbing decks.
questions.src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook-certain: naval bell-bottoms; deck-scrubbing reason is hedged with 'said to be')

questions.q: Hacky Sack, the footbag craze, was invented in 1972 in which state?
questions.fact: Friends John Stalberger and Mike Marshall created it in Oregon City; toy maker Wham-O later bought the brand.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacky_sack (invented 1972 by Mike Marshall and John Stalberger of Oregon City, Oregon; trademark sold to Wham-O in 1983)

questions.q: Walt Disney World opened in 1971 in which state?
questions.fact: It opened on October 1, 1971, with the Magic Kingdom as its only theme park.
questions.src: fox35orlando.com history of Walt Disney World (opened Oct 1, 1971); fox6now.com (Epcot opened 1982), so the Magic Kingdom was the only park at opening

questions.q: On April 8, 1974, Hank Aaron hit his 715th home run, passing which legend?
questions.fact: Aaron hit No. 715 for the Atlanta Braves off Al Downing of the Los Angeles Dodgers.
questions.src: sabr.org Games Project, April 8, 1974 (Al Downing pitching for the Los Angeles Dodgers; Aaron's Braves won)

questions.q: Which Chicago skyscraper became the world's tallest building when it opened in 1973?
questions.fact: It held the title for nearly 25 years and was renamed Willis Tower in 2009.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willis_Tower (opened Sept 1973, world's tallest at opening, ~25 years; renamed July 16, 2009)

questions.q: In 1973, which horse won the Triple Crown, taking the Belmont Stakes by 31 lengths?
questions.fact: Seattle Slew in 1977 and Affirmed in 1978 also won the Triple Crown, making three in one decade.
questions.src: si.com 'Secretariat's 31-length victory at the 1973 Belmont'; ktvb.com This Day in Sports. Seattle Slew 1977 and Affirmed 1978 Triple Crowns, Citation 1948: textbook.

blurb: Go-go boots, Touch-Tone phones and Beatlemania: the swinging 60s

questions.q: Which sporty Ford car was unveiled at the 1964 New York World's Fair?
questions.fact: It was such a hit that Ford sold more than 400,000 Mustangs in its first year.
questions.src: fromtheroad.ford.com 'Mustang launch: the grand introduction' (unveiled at the New York World's Fair, public debut April 17, 1964; 'more than 418,000 units' in the first year)

questions.q: Kodak's Instamatic camera, launched in 1963, made photography easier with what feature?
questions.fact: More than 50 million Instamatic cameras were produced between 1963 and 1970.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instamatic (1963; drop-in 126 cartridges; 50+ million 1963-1970). Checker swapped 'Built-in flash' (early Instamatics took flashbulbs in a built-in holder, arguable) for 'Zoom lens' (Instamatics had fixed lenses).

questions.q: When Bell launched push-button Touch-Tone phones in 1963, what did the buttons replace?
questions.fact: The first models had just 10 buttons; the star and pound keys were added later.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push-button_telephone (Bell introduced Touch-Tone Nov 18, 1963; Western Electric 1500 'had only ten buttons'; * and # added on the 12-button model 2500 in 1968)

questions.q: Which company introduced the compact audio cassette in 1963?
questions.fact: Engineer Lou Ottens's team developed it, and it debuted at the Berlin Radio Show in August 1963.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassette_tape (Philips introduced the Compact Cassette Aug 28, 1963 at the Berlin Radio Show; Lou Ottens led the team)

questions.q: Chubby Checker's 1960 hit kicked off which dance craze?
questions.fact: 'The Twist' hit No. 1 in 1960 and again in 1962, a rare second trip to the top.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Twist_(song) (No. 1 on Sept 19, 1960 and again from Jan 13, 1962; only song to top the chart in two separate runs until 2020)

questions.q: Harvey Ball designed the yellow smiley face in 1963 for what kind of company?
questions.fact: He reportedly earned just $45 for the design and never trademarked it.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Ball (State Mutual Life Assurance Company, 1963; earned $45; didn't trademark it)

questions.q: The lava lamp was invented in 1963 by Edward Craven Walker in which country?
questions.fact: He first sold it as the Astro lamp, and it became a decor icon of the 60s and 70s.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lava_lamp (invented by Edward Craven Walker in England in 1963; Crestworth 'launched the first Astro lava lamp in 1963')

questions.q: Designer Mary Quant, who helped popularize the miniskirt, ran her famous boutique in which city?
questions.fact: Her shop, Bazaar, opened on Chelsea's King's Road in 1955.
questions.src: londonmuseum.org.uk 'How Mary Quant revolutionised 1960s fashion' (Bazaar, King's Road, Chelsea, opened 1955)

questions.q: The Beatles' first live US TV appearance, in February 1964, was on whose show?
questions.fact: About 73 million viewers tuned in that night, February 9, 1964.
questions.src: smithsonianmag.com 'On this day in 1964, 73 million Americans tuned in'; boston25news.com 'first live US television appearance' (Feb 9, 1964). Jack Paar showed clips only.

questions.q: In July 1969, Apollo 11's lunar module, the craft that landed on the Moon, had what name?
questions.fact: Michael Collins stayed in orbit in the command module, Columbia, while Armstrong and Aldrin landed.
questions.src: si.edu newsdesk factsheet 'Apollo 11 Command Module Columbia' (CM Columbia, LM Eagle; Collins orbited while Armstrong and Aldrin landed). Falcon was Apollo 15's LM, Snoopy Apollo 10's.

questions.q: Which team, nicknamed the 'Miracle' team, won the 1969 World Series?
questions.fact: The Mets had finished ninth or tenth in every one of their first seven seasons.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_World_Series (beat the Orioles 4-1; Mets 'had never finished higher than ninth place (next-to-last)' in the 10-team NL)

questions.q: Telstar, the 1962 satellite that beamed live TV between the US and Europe, was built by which company?
questions.fact: NASA launched it on July 10, 1962, and its name later went on a famous World Cup soccer ball.
questions.src: nokia.com/bell-labs Telstar 1 story (built by AT&T Bell Telephone Laboratories, launched with NASA July 10, 1962; live TV and phone signals between US and Europe; inspired the World Cup ball). nasa.gov Telstar history (also relayed phone, data and fax).

blurb: Selfies, viral dresses and six-second videos: the 2010s

questions.q: Apple's first iPad went on sale in which year?
questions.fact: The Wi-Fi model reached US stores on April 3, 2010; the smaller iPad mini followed in 2012.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPad

questions.q: When Instagram launched in 2010, it was available only on which device?
questions.fact: Facebook bought Instagram in 2012 for about $1 billion.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram (iOS-only release Oct 6, 2010; Android April 3, 2012; Facebook bought it for $1 billion April 9, 2012)

questions.q: Apple's voice assistant Siri debuted on which iPhone model in 2011?
questions.fact: The iPhone 4S went on sale on October 14, 2011, with Siri labeled a beta feature.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siri ('On October 14, 2011, Apple launched the iPhone 4S with a beta version of Siri')

questions.q: Vine, the 2010s looping-video app, limited clips to how many seconds?
questions.fact: Twitter bought the startup in October 2012 for a reported $30 million.
questions.src: bandt.com.au 'Gone in 6 seconds: Twitter's Vine app set to close' (six-second app; acquired by Twitter Oct 2012 for a reported $30 million)

questions.q: Which 2016 mobile game sent millions of people outdoors to catch Pikachu and friends?
questions.fact: Niantic, the company that made it, began in 2010 as a startup inside Google.
questions.src: Fortune, 2016-07-12 (https://fortune.com/2016/07/12/google-pokemon-go): launched July 6, 2016; Niantic Labs founded inside Google in 2010, spun off 2015

questions.q: In 2012, which video became the first on YouTube to reach 1 billion views?
questions.fact: South Korean singer PSY's video passed the mark in December 2012.
questions.src: guinnessworldrecords.com 'First video to receive one billion views'; history.com This Day in History, Dec 21 (Gangnam Style first to 1 billion, 2012)

questions.q: Oxford Dictionaries' 2015 Word of the Year wasn't a word at all. Which emoji was it?
questions.fact: Designer Shigetaka Kurita created an early, widely used emoji set for Japanese phones in 1999.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emoji (Oxford 2015 WOTY; Kurita 1999 DoCoMo set)

questions.q: Internet sensation Grumpy Cat's real name was what?
questions.fact: She first went viral in 2012 after a photo of her was posted on Reddit.
questions.src: complex.com '30 things you didn't know about Grumpy Cat' (real name Tardar Sauce; photo posted to Reddit Sept 22, 2012). Other options are other famous internet cats.

questions.q: The Burj Khalifa became the world's tallest building when it opened in 2010. In which city?
questions.fact: It rises about 2,717 feet, more than half a mile into the sky.
questions.src: guinnessworldrecords.com tallest building (Burj Khalifa, Downtown Dubai, 828 m / 2,716 ft 6 in; opened Jan 4, 2010)

questions.q: The 'Great American Eclipse' crossed the US from Oregon to South Carolina in which year?
questions.fact: On August 21, 2017, it became the first total solar eclipse to cross the US coast to coast since 1918.
questions.src: fox2detroit.com 'Countdown begins for the Great American Eclipse' (Aug 21, 2017, Oregon to South Carolina; first coast-to-coast total eclipse since 1918)

questions.q: How did Felix Baumgartner break the sound barrier in 2012?
questions.fact: He leapt from a capsule about 24 miles up during the Red Bull Stratos project.
questions.src: itv.com / mprnews.org, Oct 14, 2012 (24-mile skydive from a balloon capsule; broke the sound barrier)

questions.q: In 2016, which club stunned soccer fans by winning England's Premier League?
questions.fact: Just a year earlier, Leicester had been fighting to avoid relegation to the second tier.
questions.src: nbcsports.com 'Leicester City crowned 2015-16 Premier League champions'; thescore.com 'Leicester City's great escape from relegation' (2014-15)
